target: tracker.sh dependents — reverse lookup, direct and transitive
cmd:
mkdir -p factory/specs; printf -- '---
id: 001
title: root
status: specd
---
body
' > factory/specs/001-a.md; printf -- '---
id: 002
title: mid
status: specd
depends_on: 001
---
body
' > factory/specs/002-b.md; printf -- '---
id: 003
title: leaf
status: queued
depends_on: 002
---
body
' > factory/specs/003-c.md; printf -- '---
id: 004
title: diamond
status: queued
depends_on: 001 002
---
body
' > factory/specs/004-d.md; printf -- '---
id: 005
title: unrelated
status: queued
---
body
' > factory/specs/005-e.md; source "$PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/lib/tracker.sh"; DIRECT="$(tracker_dependents 001 | awk -F'\t' '{print $2}' | sort | tr '\n' ',')"; TRANS="$(tracker_dependents 001 --transitive | awk -F'\t' '{print $2":"$4}' | sort | tr '\n' ',')"; NDIR="$(tracker_dependents 001 | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"; NTRANS="$(tracker_dependents 001 --transitive | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"; NONE="$(tracker_dependents 005 | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"; jq -n --arg d "$DIRECT" --arg t "$TRANS" --arg nd "$NDIR" --arg nt "$NTRANS" --arg none "$NONE" '{direct: $d, trans: $t, nd: $nd, nt: $nt, none: $none}'
_note: 004 depends on BOTH 001 and 002, so a naive walk would print it twice and the shelve skill would interview the user about the same spec twice; the dedupe is what stops that. Depth is what lets the skill order the conversation nearest-first.
